concepts.decision: Keep decisions aligned to business objectives and tolerance.
concepts.definition: Coordinate assessment, treatment, ownership, communication and review.
concepts.failureExample: A risk register is updated annually while the service changes weekly.
concepts.label: Risk Management

concepts.decision: Name the business service or information whose loss matters.
concepts.definition: Something of value to the organization or its mission.
concepts.failureExample: The server is listed but its dependency on emergency dispatch is missed.
concepts.label: Asset

concepts.decision: Identify the relevant actor, event or circumstance.
concepts.definition: A potential cause of an unwanted incident or adverse consequence.
concepts.failureExample: A fire and credential theft require different exposure analysis.
concepts.label: Threat

concepts.decision: Connect the weakness to an actual exposure path.
concepts.definition: A weakness or condition a threat can exploit.
concepts.failureExample: A vulnerable service is rated without checking whether the attack path reaches it.
concepts.label: Vulnerability

concepts.decision: Use exposure, threat capability, controls and uncertainty.
concepts.definition: An estimate of how plausible or frequent the scenario is in context.
concepts.failureExample: Historical silence is treated as evidence that exploitation is impossible.
concepts.label: Likelihood

concepts.decision: Assess financial, operational, legal, safety and other relevant harm.
concepts.definition: The consequence if the scenario occurs.
concepts.failureExample: Low replacement cost hides a high cost of lost business service.
concepts.label: Impact

concepts.decision: Identify the owner and threshold that will determine treatment.
concepts.definition: Evaluate the scenario, likelihood, impact and uncertainty against decision criteria.
concepts.failureExample: A qualitative label is presented with spurious numerical precision.
concepts.label: Risk Assessment

concepts.decision: Assign owners, resources, intended effect and success evidence.
concepts.definition: Select and implement one or more responses to the assessed scenario.
concepts.failureExample: A treatment is listed without implementation responsibility or a deadline.
concepts.label: Risk Treatment

concepts.decision: Check delegated authority, tolerance, duration and review trigger.
concepts.definition: An authorized owner knowingly retains the exposure under defined conditions.
concepts.failureExample: An engineer silently waives a high-impact control without approval.
concepts.label: Risk Acceptance

concepts.decision: Check scope, exclusions, counterparty capability and retained duties.
concepts.definition: Allocate specified consequences through insurance, contract or another arrangement.
concepts.failureExample: An insurance policy pays certain losses but does not restore customer trust.
concepts.label: Risk Transfer

concepts.decision: Compare the forgone business benefit with the exposure avoided.
concepts.definition: Stop or decline the activity producing the specified exposure.
concepts.failureExample: Cancel the sensitive-data collection instead of protecting unnecessary records.
concepts.label: Risk Avoidance

concepts.decision: Choose effective, proportionate controls and verify operation.
concepts.definition: Reduce likelihood, impact, or both with safeguards.
concepts.failureExample: Segmentation limits propagation but does not eliminate all compromise paths.
concepts.label: Risk Mitigation

concepts.decision: Evaluate whether the remaining exposure meets acceptance criteria.
concepts.definition: Exposure remaining after treatment is considered.
concepts.failureExample: Deploying a control is mistaken for proving that the remaining risk is acceptable.
concepts.label: Residual Risk

concepts.decision: Choose the function needed for the failure path and combine functions.
concepts.definition: Preventive controls inhibit events; detective controls reveal them; corrective controls address resulting conditions.
concepts.failureExample: An alerting dashboard is counted as prevention without an enforcement action.
concepts.label: Control Types

concepts.decision: Trigger review when exposure, control performance or context changes.
concepts.definition: Gather and assess signals at a risk-appropriate cadence.
concepts.failureExample: New privileged accounts are ignored until the next annual audit.
concepts.label: Continuous Monitoring

concepts.decision: Define scope, test method, evidence period and limitations.
concepts.definition: Evaluate whether controls are designed, implemented and operating adequately.
concepts.failureExample: A configured backup job is accepted without testing a restore.
concepts.label: Control Assessment

concepts.decision: State the decision needed rather than only activity counts.
concepts.definition: Communicate exposure, uncertainty, action and ownership to the decision audience.
concepts.failureExample: A report shows alerts closed but hides an overdue high-risk exception.
concepts.label: Reporting

concepts.decision: Use trends and context to judge effectiveness and improvement.
concepts.definition: Measures with a defined population, method, period, owner and intended use.
concepts.failureExample: A low incident count is treated as proof of strong detection.
concepts.label: Security Metrics

misconceptions.claim: A high-level risk is eliminated when any new control is purchased.
misconceptions.correction: Controls need implementation, assessment, residual-risk evaluation, monitoring, and an owner decision.

misconceptions.claim: Continuous monitoring proves a control is effective.
misconceptions.correction: Monitoring provides signals; a scoped assessment must still test whether the control meets its objective and reduces the relevant risk.

outcome: Analyze a risk statement, distinguish treatment choices, and recommend the accountable next step with evidence.

sections.body: A useful risk analysis scopes an asset or objective, threat event, vulnerability or exposure, existing controls, likelihood, impact, uncertainty, and owner. Likelihood considers more than adversary intent; exposure, capability, opportunity, and control effectiveness matter. Impact considers business, legal, financial, safety, privacy, and mission consequences. Qualitative ratings are useful only when their terms are defined and applied consistently.
keyPoints: A risk score summarizes judgment; it does not replace the underlying scenario.
Threat, vulnerability, and impact are different parts of a risk statement.
sections.title: Analyze a scenario, not a label

sections.body: An organization can avoid an activity, mitigate likelihood or impact with controls, transfer or share specified consequences, or accept residual risk within authorized tolerance. Preventive, detective, corrective, deterrent, compensating, and recovery controls serve different purposes and need assessment. Monitoring and reporting test whether assumptions and controls remain valid; continuous improvement responds to changed threats, business priorities, incidents, and measurements.
keyPoints: Insurance may transfer some financial consequence but does not remove operational risk.
Control assessment and monitoring are part of treatment, not paperwork after treatment.
sections.title: Treat and monitor residual risk

sections.body: Identify threats and vulnerabilities for a defined asset, process, or objective; scope the assessment, evaluate likelihood, impact, uncertainty, existing controls, and residual risk; then select avoidance, mitigation, transfer or sharing such as insurance, or accountable acceptance. Match preventive, detective, and corrective controls to the failure path, assess security and privacy controls, continuously monitor signals and changes, report to internal and external audiences as required, and use findings to improve maturity. ISO, NIST, COBIT, SABSA, PCI, and related frameworks organize the work but do not replace risk ownership. Failure occurs when a score obscures assumptions, a control is selected without assessment, insurance is mistaken for prevention, or acceptance lacks authority and expiry.
keyPoints: Name the accountable owner, decision criterion, and evidence for each applicable outline topic.
Record the failure consequence and escalation or review trigger rather than assuming a policy label proves operation.
sections.title: Operate an evidence-driven risk-management cycle

sections.body: A control assessment asks whether the control is correctly designed, implemented, operating as intended, and still adequate for the risk scenario and applicable privacy requirements. Define the control objective, owner, test method, evidence period, exceptions, result, residual risk, remediation owner, and due date. Monitoring supplies current signals; reporting converts them into decision-ready information for the accountable audience. A dashboard that lists activity without scope, threshold, trend, consequence, and owner is not useful risk reporting.
keyPoints: Assessment verifies a claimed control; monitoring detects change between assessments.
Report risk in the audience’s decision terms: exposure, consequence, uncertainty, treatment, residual risk, and action needed.
An implemented control can still be ineffective, out of scope, or obsolete.
sections.title: Verify the control and report the decision

sections.body: A risk measure should answer a management question and have a defined owner, population, method, threshold, cadence, limitation, and action when it crosses a trigger. Examples include time to detect/contain a specified event, percentage of material assets with current risk decisions, aging of high-risk exceptions, or validated control coverage. Compare a baseline to a later result in context; do not infer maturity from a single low incident count. ISO 31000, ISO/IEC 27005, NIST risk guidance, COBIT, SABSA, and PCI-related methods can structure work, but the organization must select and tailor a framework to its decisions and obligations.
keyPoints: A KPI measures a process or outcome only if its population and decision use are explicit.
Maturity is demonstrated by repeatable, evidenced improvement, not a framework name.
Choose a framework that fits scope and stakeholders; retain accountable risk ownership.
sections.title: Use measures to improve a risk process, not merely to count activity

summary: Risk management identifies and analyzes uncertainty affecting objectives, selects an authorized treatment, verifies controls, monitors change, reports residual risk, and improves the process over time.

assumptions: Only entities and claims anchored in the canonical unit or explicitly labeled hypothetical scenario are used.
A highlighted path means the learner is inspecting that path; it does not assert the event occurred.
The current source is authoritative for facts; this treatment reorganizes presentation without changing canonical content.
The lesson teaches one bounded decision and does not claim to exhaust every jurisdiction, vendor implementation, architecture, attack, or exception.

teaching.focalRelation: Asset/objective plus threat event plus vulnerability/exposure yields a scenario; controls modify likelihood or impact only within evidenced scope; assessment tests the claim, monitoring detects change, and an authorized owner decides residual risk.

learningJob.plainExplanation: Risk belongs to a defined loss scenario, not a generic dashboard color. Evidence changes likelihood or impact only in scope, and an authorized owner decides treatment and residual risk with a review trigger.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: A loop can coordinate scenario, evidence, treatment, assurance, decision, and reassessment; isolated selected edges force the learner to rebuild the loop mentally.

title: Make risk treatment an accountable, continuous decision

workedExamples.reasoning: Scope the dispatch outcome, identify threat and exposure, assess likelihood and impact, choose controls and recovery improvements, assign residual-risk ownership, and define monitoring and reassessment triggers.
workedExamples.situation: A transit authority relies on an unsegmented operational network and has uncertain restoration dependencies.
workedExamples.takeaway: Deploying one backup appliance may reduce risk but does not establish that the scenario is treated.
workedExamples.title: Ransomware and dispatch

workedExamples.reasoning: Define the control objective and test sample: logging completeness, alert generation, review timeliness, escalation evidence, and remediation closure. Report the resulting residual risk and decision request to the accountable owner. Track a defined measure such as high-risk alert review within the target window and reassess after process change.
workedExamples.situation: A monthly report shows that privileged-access logs are collected, but the team cannot show who reviewed high-risk events or whether alerts worked.
workedExamples.takeaway: Data collection becomes risk evidence only when it supports a defined control claim and management action.
workedExamples.title: Privileged-access logging gap
